title: The smaller-support induction step for a universally injective free submodule
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with geometrically integral fibres of dimension $n\geq0$ (each fibre remains nonzero and integral after any residue-field extension), and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ a prime above $\mathfrak m$. Let $N,Q$ be finite $B$-modules and let $0\to B^r\xrightarrow{\alpha}N\to Q\to0$ be an exact sequence, $r\geq0$, with $\alpha$ universally injective over $A$, meaning $L\otimes_A\alpha$ is injective for every $A$-module $L$. Suppose $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $A$, and either $(Q/\mathfrak mQ)_{\mathfrak q}=0$ or the dimension at $\mathfrak q$ of the support of $Q/\mathfrak mQ$ is $<n$ [def-kun-dimension]. Assume the following smaller-support hypothesis: for every finite $B$-module $M$ such that $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat, $(M/\mathfrak mM)_{\mathfrak q}\ne0$, and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Supp}(M/\mathfrak mM)<n$, there exist an affine elementary etale neighbourhood $(T,t)$ of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and an open neighbourhood of the marked point of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\mathcal O_{T,t})$ on which the associated sheaf of $M\otimes_A\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is finitely presented and flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Elementary etale means etale with an isomorphism of residue fields at the marked points [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-residue-field]. Then there exist such $(T,t)$, $A'=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $B'=B\otimes_A A'$, and $g\in B'\setminus\mathfrak q'$, where $\mathfrak q'$ is the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}B'$ above $\mathfrak q$, such that $Q'_g$ and $N'_g$ are finitely presented $B'_g$-modules and flat $A'$-modules, with $N'=N\otimes_A A'$ and $Q'=Q\otimes_A A'$. The sequence $0\to(B'_g)^r\to N'_g\to Q'_g\to0$ is exact, and the associated sheaf of $N'$ restricted to $D(g)$ is finitely presented and flat over $A'$. If $(Q/\mathfrak mQ)_{\mathfrak q}=0$, one may take $A'=A$ and $Q_g=0$, without using the smaller-support hypothesis. Finite modules, finite presentation, flatness, module localization, tensor products, open subschemes and the associated sheaf have their meanings in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-sc-finitely-presented-module, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-module-localization, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-open-immersion, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation, def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. The associated sheaf of a module $M$ over a commutative ring $R$ is the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-module $\widetilde M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. Support means nonzero localizations.

proof.text: First suppose $(Q/\mathfrak mQ)_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Exact localization identifies this module with $Q_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak mB_{\mathfrak q}Q_{\mathfrak q}$. The finite module $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ and the ideal $\mathfrak mB_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$ satisfy Nakayama over the local ring $B_{\mathfrak q}$, so $Q_{\mathfrak q}=0$. Choose finite generators $z_1,\ldots,z_s$ of $Q$. By the definition of localization ($m/1=0$ iff some element of the multiplicative set kills $m$), for each $i$ some $h_i\notin\mathfrak q$ kills $z_i$. The product $g=\prod_i h_i\notin\mathfrak q$ kills all of $Q$; for $s=0$ use $g=1$. Take the identity elementary etale neighbourhood, so $A\prime=A$ and $Q_g=0$. The zero module is finitely presented and flat. This branch has not used induction. In the remaining steps this choice is treated together with the nonzero-fibre branch.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, zero-cokernel boundary of the induction; Algebra Tags 00CS and 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: If $(Q/\mathfrak mQ)_{\mathfrak q}\ne0$, apply the stated smaller-support hypothesis to $M=Q$: finiteness, flatness at $\mathfrak q$, and the strict dimension inequality are exactly the assumptions. Obtain $(T,t)$ and its open neighbourhood $V$ of the marked point. The one-step case of the pointed etale local-tower lemma identifies the fibre above $\mathfrak q$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; hence this marked point is the unique $\mathfrak q\prime$ in the statement. Choose $g\notin\mathfrak q\prime$ with $D(g)\subseteq V$ by the principal-open basis. Restriction of a local finite presentation is still a local finite presentation, directly by restricting its finite free presentation maps. Principal-open sections of the associated sheaf of $Q\prime$ are $Q\prime_g$ (use the associated-sections lemma with both rings equal to $B\prime$). The affine finite-presentation equivalence therefore makes $Q\prime_g$ finitely presented over $B\prime_g$. Flatness over $A\prime$ on $V$ gives flatness of these affine sections by the definition of relative flatness. Thus in both branches we now have $A\prime$, $g$, and finitely presented, $A\prime$-flat $Q\prime_g$.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, application of the smaller-support hypothesis and choice of a principal open

proof.text: Smoothness makes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ flat. By the definition of a flat morphism each stalk $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathfrak p\cap A}$, and the stalk-localization lemma identifies these stalks with $B_{\mathfrak p}$ and $A_{\mathfrak p\cap A}$, compatibly with the structure map; so each $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p\cap A}$; the affine-sections flatness criterion gives that $B$ is $A$-flat. Base change of this flat module shows $B\prime=B\otimes_AA\prime$ is $A\prime$-flat. Localizing the $B\prime$-module $B\prime$ preserves flatness over $A\prime$, so $B\prime_g$ is $A\prime$-flat. Finally $(B\prime_g)^r$ is $A\prime$-flat: tensoring an injection with it is the finite direct sum of $r$ injections obtained by tensoring with $B\prime_g$. This also covers $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, flatness of the localized free term

proof.text: Tensor the original exact sequence over $A$ with $A\prime$. Right exactness gives exactness at $N\prime$ and $Q\prime$, and universal injectivity of $\alpha$ with $L=A\prime$ gives injectivity at $(B\prime)^r$. Exact localization then gives $0\to(B\prime_g)^r\xrightarrow a N\prime_g\xrightarrow v Q\prime_g\to0$. We will also use its universal injectivity over $A\prime$: for any $A\prime$-module $L$, the maps $L\otimes_{A\prime}(A\prime\otimes_A B^r)\to L\otimes_{A\prime}(A\prime\otimes_A N)$ identify with $L\otimes_A\alpha$, which is injective by assumption. After localizing over $B\prime$, injectivity persists by exact localization. The needed tensor/localization comparison sends $(l\otimes n)/g^j$ to $l\otimes(n/g^j)$, with inverse $l\otimes(n/g^j)\mapsto(l\otimes n)/g^j$; the bilinearity and fraction relations show both maps are well-defined and inverse. Hence $L\otimes_{A\prime}a$ is injective for every $L$. These identifications also give $(B\prime)^r$ as the tensor of $B^r$, coordinate by coordinate.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, base change and exact localization of the free-submodule sequence

proof.text: Set $R=B\prime_g$. Exactness identifies $\ker(v)$ with $R^r$ by $a$: every element of the kernel is $a(x)$, and $a(x)=0$ implies $x=0$. The free module $R^r$ is finitely presented by the presentation $R^0\to R^r\to R^r\to0$; an isomorphism transports this presentation to $\ker(v)$. Since $Q\prime_g$ is finitely presented and $v$ is surjective, apply the finite-presentation-of-kernel criterion with $M=N\prime_g$ and $P=Q\prime_g$. It follows that $N\prime_g$ is finitely presented over $R$.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, finite presentation of the middle module; Algebra Tag 0519, lemma-extension (2)

proof.text: Here is the flat-extension argument, written out over $A\prime$. Put $F=(B\prime_g)^r$, $E=N\prime_g$, and $C=Q\prime_g$. For an injection $u:L\to L_1$, take $z\in L\otimes E$ mapping to zero in $L_1\otimes E$. Its image in $L\otimes C$ is zero, because $C$ is flat. Right exactness gives $y\in L\otimes F$ with image $z$. The image of $y$ in $L_1\otimes F$ maps to zero in $L_1\otimes E$, so is zero by the universal injectivity proved in step 4. Flatness of $F$ gives $y=0$, hence $z=0$. Thus $u\otimes1_E$ is injective for every injection $u$. Tensoring is right exact, so this injectivity says that tensoring with $E$ preserves exact sequences: $N\prime_g$ is $A\prime$-flat. This is the elementary tensor chase for Algebra Tag 00HM, using the universal injectivity present in this item.

source.place: Tag 05I5, proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point, first proof, flatness of the middle module; explicit form of the Algebra Tag 00HM argument

proof.text: On $D(g)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\prime_g)$ the associated sheaf of $N\prime$ has principal-open sections $(N\prime_g)_h$ for every $h\in B\prime_g$, by the associated-sections localization formula. The affine finite-presentation equivalence turns finite presentation of $N\prime_g$ into finite presentation of this sheaf. For a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $B\prime$ in $D(g)$, the stalk of $\widetilde{N\prime}$ at $\mathfrak p$ is $N\prime_{\mathfrak p}=(N\prime_g)_{\mathfrak p}$ by the stalk-localization lemma for $\widetilde{N\prime}$, and the stalk of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A\prime}$ at $\mathfrak p\cap A\prime$ is $A\prime_{\mathfrak p\cap A\prime}$ by the structure-sheaf stalk lemma. Each localization $(N\prime_g)_{\mathfrak p}$ remains flat over $A\prime$ by preservation of base-flatness under module localization. The flat-over-localization equivalence, with multiplicative subset $A\prime\setminus(\mathfrak p\cap A\prime)$, then shows this stalk is flat over $A\prime_{\mathfrak p\cap A\prime}$. The stalk formulation of relative flatness proves that the sheaf is flat over $\operatorname{Spec}A\prime$. The exact sequence and both module properties were proved above, so all conclusions follow, including the choice $A\prime=A$, $Q_g=0$ in the zero-fibre branch.
